# Fabric Attach Zero-Touch Client NetLogin Bypass Enhancement
## EXOS-39369 QA Testing Skill File

**JIRA Story**: EXOS-39369  
**Feature**: Fabric Attach Zero-Touch Client with NetLogin Bypass  
**EXOS Version**: 33.7+ (34.1)  
**Platform Support**: All EXOS platforms  
**Generated by**: GitHub Copilot (Claude Sonnet 4.6)  
**Date**: 2026-07-23

---

## 1. FEATURE SUMMARY

### 1.1 Overview
This enhancement adds a `bypass-netlogin` configuration option to Fabric Attach (FA) zero-touch-client configuration, enabling FA devices to bypass NetLogin MAC-based authentication while still receiving their configured VLAN/NSI assignments.

### 1.2 Business Context
**Problem Solved**: In environments with both Fabric Attach and NetLogin enabled, FA devices previously required NetLogin authentication before attachment. This creates deployment friction for trusted infrastructure devices (switches, IP phones, cameras) that should have seamless zero-touch provisioning.

**Solution Provided**: The `bypass-netlogin` option allows administrators to selectively exempt FA client types from NetLogin authentication while maintaining authentication requirements for other endpoints.

### 1.3 Key Capabilities
- ✅ Per-client-type bypass configuration
- ✅ Maintains zero-touch VLAN/NSI assignment behavior
- ✅ Works with all FA client types (switch, server, ip-phone, camera, router, security-device)
- ✅ Enhanced visibility in show commands
- ✅ Backward compatible (defaults to OFF - authentication required)

---

## 2. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

### 2.1 Component Interaction Flow

```
[FA Device] ──LLDP──> [EXOS Switch Proxy]
                            │
                            ├──> FA Subsystem: Discovers device + client type
                            │
                            ├──> Check: bypass-netlogin enabled?
                            │         │
                            │         ├─ NO ──> NetLogin: Authenticate MAC
                            │         │              │
                            │         │              ├─ Success ──> Attach + Apply VLAN
                            │         │              └─ Fail ──> Block attachment
                            │         │
                            │         └─ YES ──> Skip auth ──> Attach + Apply VLAN
                            │
                            └──> Update show commands
```

### 2.2 Subsystem Coordination

| Subsystem | Role | Data Exchanged |
|-----------|------|----------------|
| **LLDP** | Discovery | FA TLVs, device info, client type |
| **Fabric Attach** | Zero-touch provisioning | Client type, VLAN/I-SID mappings |
| **NetLogin** | Authentication (conditional) | MAC address, auth result, bypass list |
| **VLAN** | Network assignment | VLAN ID, port membership |
| **Forwarding** | Traffic handling | MAC learning, forwarding state |

**Key Integration Point**: LLDP communicates bypass clients to NetLogin subsystem, which maintains a bypass list even when NetLogin is disabled on the port.

### 2.3 Authentication Decision Matrix

| Port NetLogin State | bypass-netlogin Setting | Device Authentication | FA Attachment | Display Status |
|---------------------|------------------------|----------------------|---------------|----------------|
| Enabled | OFF (default) | Required | Only if auth succeeds | N/A or No |
| Enabled | ON | Bypassed | Immediate | Yes |
| Disabled | OFF | N/A | Immediate | N/A |
| Disabled | ON | N/A | Immediate | N/A |

## 3. CONFIGURATION GUIDE

### 3.1 CLI Command Syntax

#### Enable NetLogin Bypass
```bash
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client <client-type> bypass-netlogin [on | off]
```

**Parameters**:
- `<client-type>`: switch | server | router | ip-phone | camera | security-device
- `on`: Enable bypass (device skips NetLogin authentication)
- `off`: Disable bypass (device requires authentication) - **DEFAULT**

**Example**:
```bash
# Enable bypass for IP phones
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone bypass-netlogin on

# Enable bypass for switches  
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch bypass-netlogin on

# Disable bypass for cameras (require authentication)
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera bypass-netlogin off
```

#### Unconfigure Command
```bash
unconfigure fabric attach zero-touch-client <client-type> bypass-netlogin
```
**Effect**: Returns to default behavior (OFF - authentication required)

### 3.2 Complete Configuration Examples

#### Example 1: Mixed Security Posture
**Scenario**: Trust infrastructure devices (switches, phones), authenticate endpoints (cameras, servers)

```bash
# Enable NetLogin globally
enable netlogin mac

# Configure FA zero-touch clients with VLAN assignments
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch vlan voice-vlan i-sid 16777301
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone vlan voice-vlan i-sid 16777301
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera vlan camera-vlan i-sid 16777302
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client server vlan data-vlan i-sid 16777303

# Enable bypass for trusted infrastructure
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch bypass-netlogin on
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone bypass-netlogin on

# Cameras and servers require authentication (default OFF - no command needed)
# But explicitly set for clarity:
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera bypass-netlogin off
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client server bypass-netlogin off

# Enable NetLogin on edge ports
configure netlogin add mac-list ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
enable netlogin ports 1:1-1:24 mac
```

**Result**:
- FA switches and IP phones: Bypass authentication, immediate attachment
- FA cameras and servers: Must authenticate before attachment
- Non-FA devices: Standard NetLogin authentication applies

#### Example 2: Zero-Touch Campus Deployment
**Scenario**: Rapid deployment of FA infrastructure without authentication barriers

```bash
# Enable FA in proxy mode
enable fabric attach

# Configure all FA client types with bypass
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch vlan default i-sid 16777216 bypass-netlogin on
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone vlan voice i-sid 16777220 bypass-netlogin on
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera vlan camera i-sid 16777221 bypass-netlogin on
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client security-device vlan security i-sid 16777222 bypass-netlogin on

# NetLogin still enabled for non-FA devices
enable netlogin mac
```

**Result**: All FA devices bypass authentication, non-FA devices still require NetLogin

#### Example 3: Secure Environment (No Bypass)
**Scenario**: High-security network requiring authentication for all devices

```bash
# Configure FA zero-touch clients
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch vlan default i-sid 16777216
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client server vlan data i-sid 16777217

# Explicitly disable bypass (default behavior)
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch bypass-netlogin off
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client server bypass-netlogin off

# Enable NetLogin with RADIUS backend
configure netlogin authentication protocol-order dot1x mac
enable netlogin ports all
```

**Result**: All FA devices require NetLogin authentication before attachment

#### Example 4: Selective Port Bypass
**Scenario**: IDF closets use bypass, desk ports require authentication

```bash
# IDF uplink ports (trusted FA switches)
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch bypass-netlogin on
enable fabric attach ports 1:1-1:4  # Uplink ports

# Desk ports (untrusted devices)
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client server bypass-netlogin off
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera bypass-netlogin off
enable fabric attach ports 1:5-1:48  # User ports
enable netlogin ports 1:5-1:48 mac
```

- `Yes`: bypass-netlogin is ON, device bypassed authentication

### 4.3 Operational Verification Tests

#### Test 1: Bypass Enabled - Successful Attachment
**Setup**:
```bash
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch bypass-netlogin on
enable netlogin ports 1:1 mac
```

**Test Steps**:
1. Connect FA switch to port 1:1
2. Wait 30 seconds for LLDP discovery

**Expected Result**:
```bash
show fabric attach elements
# Should show: Port 1:1, Type Switch, Netlogin Bypass: Yes

show netlogin
# Should show: Bypass client on port 1:1
```

**Verification**: Device attached without NetLogin authentication attempt

#### Test 2: Bypass Disabled - Authentication Required
**Setup**:
```bash
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera bypass-netlogin off
enable netlogin ports 1:2 mac
configure netlogin add mac-list 00:04:96:aa:bb:cc  # Camera MAC
```

**Test Steps**:
1. Connect FA camera (MAC 00:04:96:aa:bb:cc) to port 1:2
2. Wait for LLDP discovery + NetLogin auth

**Expected Result**:
```bash
show fabric attach elements
# Should show: Port 1:2, Type Camera, Netlogin Bypass: No

show netlogin
# Should show: Authenticated client on port 1:2 (NOT in bypass list)
```

**Verification**: Device attached only after successful NetLogin authentication

#### Test 3: Bypass Setting Change During Operation
**Setup**:
```bash
# Start with bypass enabled
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone bypass-netlogin on
# Device already attached on port 1:3
```

**Test Steps**:
1. Verify current attachment: `show fabric attach elements port 1:3`
2. Change setting: `configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone bypass-netlogin off`
3. Disconnect and reconnect device

**Expected Result**:
- Before change: Netlogin Bypass = Yes
- After reconnect: Netlogin Bypass = No (requires authentication)

**Verification**: Setting change takes effect on new device connections

## 5. FEATURE INTERACTIONS

### 5.1 NetLogin Integration

#### Authentication Flow Coordination
**When NetLogin Enabled + Bypass OFF**:
1. LLDP discovers FA device
2. FA subsystem identifies client type
3. FA signals NetLogin: "Device requires authentication"
4. NetLogin performs MAC-based auth
5. On success: FA attaches device, applies VLAN/I-SID
6. On failure: Device blocked, no FA attachment

**When NetLogin Enabled + Bypass ON**:
1. LLDP discovers FA device
2. FA subsystem identifies client type
3. FA signals NetLogin: "Device is bypass client"
4. NetLogin adds to bypass list, skips authentication
5. FA immediately attaches device, applies VLAN/I-SID

#### NetLogin Subsystem State
- NetLogin maintains bypass client list even when disabled
- Bypass list persists across NetLogin enable/disable cycles
- Bypass clients excluded from NetLogin session counts

### 5.2 LLDP Communication

**LLDP TLV Processing**:
- LLDP receives FA TLVs with Element Type, System ID
- Element Type maps to FA client type (5=Switch, 9=IP Phone, 10=Camera, etc.)
- Client type lookup determines bypass-netlogin setting
- LLDP notifies NetLogin of bypass clients

**Timing Considerations**:
- LLDP advertisement interval: 30 seconds (default)
- FA discovery time: 30-90 seconds
- NetLogin authentication time: 2-10 seconds (RADIUS-dependent)
- Bypass device attachment time: 30-35 seconds (no auth delay)

### 5.3 VLAN Assignment Interaction

**VLAN Application Sequence**:
1. FA zero-touch-client config defines VLAN/I-SID mapping
2. Bypass-netlogin determines authentication requirement
3. Upon successful auth (or bypass), FA applies VLAN assignment
4. Port transitions to forwarding state

**Conflict Resolution**:
- FA zero-touch VLAN takes precedence over NetLogin VLAN assignment
- If NetLogin assigns VLAN X, but FA config specifies VLAN Y: VLAN Y applied
- Bypass setting only affects authentication, not VLAN assignment logic

### 5.4 Client Type Support Matrix

| Client Type | Element Type Code | Bypass Support | Typical Use Case |
|-------------|-------------------|----------------|------------------|
| Switch | 5 | ✅ Yes | IDF/MDF switches |
| Server | 6 (Auth) / 7 (No Auth) | ✅ Yes (Auth only) | Data center servers |
| IP Phone | 9 | ✅ Yes | VoIP phones |
| Camera | 10 | ✅ Yes | IP cameras |
| Router | 4 | ✅ Yes | Branch routers |
| Security-Device | 8 | ✅ Yes | Firewalls, IPS |

**Note**: Element Type 7 (Server - No Auth) displays "N/A" for bypass status in show commands

### 5.5 High Availability Considerations

**Standby Switch Synchronization**:
- Bypass-netlogin configuration synced to standby
- Bypass client list synced via checkpoint mechanism
- Failover preserves bypass state for active sessions

**Failure Scenarios**:
- If primary fails during FA discovery: Standby continues with synced bypass config
- If LLDP link flaps: Device re-authenticated if bypass OFF, immediate reattach if bypass ON
- If NetLogin backend (RADIUS) fails: Bypass clients unaffected, non-bypass clients blocked

## 6. TESTING STRATEGY

### 6.1 Functional Test Coverage

#### TC-01: Basic Bypass Enable/Disable
**Objective**: Verify bypass-netlogin command syntax and configuration storage

**Steps**:
1. Configure bypass ON for switch client type
2. Verify configuration stored: `show configuration`
3. Configure bypass OFF
4. Verify configuration updated
5. Unconfigure bypass
6. Verify default behavior (OFF)

**Expected**: All commands accepted, configuration correctly stored and displayed

#### TC-02: Authentication Bypass Verification
**Objective**: Confirm devices bypass NetLogin when enabled

**Steps**:
1. Enable NetLogin on port without any MAC entries in MAC list
2. Enable bypass for client type
3. Connect FA device of that client type
4. Verify device attaches without auth failure logs

**Expected**: Device attaches successfully, no NetLogin auth attempts logged

#### TC-03: Authentication Required Verification
**Objective**: Confirm devices require auth when bypass disabled

**Steps**:
1. Enable NetLogin on port
2. Disable bypass for client type (or leave default OFF)
3. Connect FA device without MAC in NetLogin list
4. Verify device blocked

**Expected**: Device does not attach, NetLogin logs authentication failure

#### TC-04: Multiple Client Types
**Objective**: Verify independent bypass settings per client type

**Steps**:
1. Configure bypass ON for switch, OFF for camera
2. Connect switch to port 1:1
3. Connect camera to port 1:2
4. Verify switch bypasses, camera requires auth

**Expected**: Switch: Bypass=Yes, Camera: Bypass=No (after auth)

#### TC-05: Show Command Accuracy
**Objective**: Verify "Netlogin Bypass" column displays correctly

**Steps**:
1. Configure mixed bypass settings
2. Connect devices with various configurations
3. Verify `show fabric attach elements` displays correct Yes/No/N/A
4. Verify `show netlogin` lists bypass clients

**Expected**: All display values match configured bypass settings

#### TC-06: Dynamic Configuration Change
**Objective**: Verify bypass setting changes affect new connections

**Steps**:
1. Start with bypass ON, connect device
2. Change to bypass OFF
3. Disconnect and reconnect device
4. Verify new behavior (auth required)

**Expected**: First connection bypasses, second connection requires auth

#### TC-07: NetLogin Disabled Scenario
**Objective**: Verify bypass setting when NetLogin disabled

**Steps**:
1. Configure bypass ON for client type
2. Disable NetLogin on port
3. Connect FA device
4. Verify Netlogin Bypass column shows "N/A"

**Expected**: Device attaches (no NetLogin), Bypass status = N/A

### 6.2 Negative Test Cases

#### TC-NEG-01: Invalid Client Type
**Test**: `configure fabric attach zero-touch-client invalid-type bypass-netlogin on`  
**Expected**: Error - "Invalid client type"

#### TC-NEG-02: Invalid Bypass Value
**Test**: `configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch bypass-netlogin maybe`  
**Expected**: Error - "Invalid value, use on or off"

#### TC-NEG-03: Authentication Failure with Bypass OFF
**Test**: Connect device without MAC in NetLogin list, bypass OFF  
**Expected**: Device blocked, NetLogin logs auth failure, FA attachment fails

#### TC-NEG-04: Rapid LLDP Link Flap
**Test**: Connect/disconnect device 10 times in 60 seconds  
**Expected**: Bypass state consistent, no state corruption, all connections handled correctly

### 6.3 Performance and Scale Testing

#### TC-PERF-01: Bypass Client Scale
**Objective**: Verify 100+ bypass clients

**Steps**:
1. Configure bypass ON for all client types
2. Connect 100+ FA devices across 48 ports
3. Verify all appear in bypass list
4. Check memory and CPU usage

**Expected**: All devices attach, no performance degradation

#### TC-PERF-02: Bypass List Update Time
**Objective**: Measure time from LLDP discovery to bypass list update

**Steps**:
1. Enable logging and timestamps
2. Connect FA device with bypass enabled
3. Measure time between "LLDP advertisement received" and "Bypass client added"

**Expected**: < 5 seconds

#### TC-PERF-03: Authentication Bypass Throughput
**Objective**: Compare attachment time with/without bypass

**Steps**:
1. Test 1: Connect 10 devices with bypass ON, measure total attachment time
2. Test 2: Connect 10 devices with bypass OFF (with NetLogin), measure total time
3. Calculate time savings

**Expected**: Bypass reduces attachment time by 2-10 seconds per device (no RADIUS delay)

### 6.4 Interoperability Testing

#### TC-INTEROP-01: Mixed EXOS Versions
**Test**: Proxy switch on 33.7+, client switches on 31.7  
**Expected**: Bypass works on proxy, clients unaware of feature

#### TC-INTEROP-02: Third-Party FA Devices
**Test**: Non-EXOS FA devices (IP phones, cameras)  
**Expected**: Bypass applies based on Element Type in LLDP TLV

#### TC-INTEROP-03: RADIUS Server Integration
**Test**: Bypass ON clients + standard NetLogin clients with RADIUS  
**Expected**: Bypass clients skip RADIUS, standard clients authenticate normally

- [ ] NetLogin authentication for non-FA devices works

## 7. TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

### 7.1 Common Issues and Resolutions

#### Issue 1: Device Not Bypassing Authentication
**Symptoms**:
- bypass-netlogin configured ON
- Device still appears to require NetLogin authentication
- "Netlogin Bypass" shows "No" instead of "Yes"

**Diagnosis**:
```bash
# Check bypass configuration
show fabric attach zero-touch-client

# Check device client type in LLDP
show lldp neighbors detail

# Check actual bypass status
show fabric attach elements
```

**Possible Causes**:
1. **Client type mismatch**: LLDP Element Type doesn't match configured client type
   - **Solution**: Verify LLDP Element Type, configure correct client type
   
2. **Bypass not enabled**: Configuration not saved or applied
   - **Solution**: Re-apply configuration, verify with `show configuration`
   
3. **NetLogin authentication succeeded**: Device authenticated, bypass not needed
   - **Solution**: Check `show netlogin` - if device authenticated, bypass irrelevant
   
4. **Old LLDP advertisement cached**: Device discovered before bypass enabled
   - **Solution**: Bounce port or wait for LLDP refresh (30 sec)

#### Issue 2: Bypass Clients Shown in NetLogin Sessions
**Symptoms**:
- Device configured with bypass ON
- Device appears in `show netlogin` authenticated sessions
- Confusion about bypass vs. authenticated state

**Diagnosis**:
```bash
# Check bypass client list specifically
show netlogin | include "Bypass Clients" -A 20

# Check fabric attach bypass status
show fabric attach elements | include "Bypass"
```

**Resolution**:
- This is informational only - bypass clients shown in NetLogin context for visibility
- "Netlogin Bypass Clients" section separate from "Authenticated Sessions"
- If device appears in Authenticated Sessions (not Bypass Clients), bypass not active

#### Issue 3: Configuration Not Persistent After Reboot
**Symptoms**:
- bypass-netlogin configured
- After reboot, setting reverts to default (OFF)

**Diagnosis**:
```bash
# Check saved configuration
show configuration fabric attach | include bypass-netlogin
```

**Resolution**:
```bash
# Save configuration
save configuration
```

**Prevention**: Always save after configuration changes

#### Issue 4: "N/A" Displayed for Bypass Status
**Symptoms**:
- bypass-netlogin configured ON
- "Netlogin Bypass" column shows "N/A"

**Possible Causes**:
1. **NetLogin disabled on port**: Bypass setting displayed but not applicable
   - **Resolution**: Enable NetLogin on port to activate bypass
   
2. **Server client type = "No Auth" (Element Type 7)**: Bypass not supported
   - **Resolution**: Use Element Type 6 (Server - Auth) if bypass needed
   
3. **Device not yet discovered**: LLDP discovery in progress
   - **Resolution**: Wait 30-60 seconds for LLDP advertisement

### 7.2 Debug Commands

#### Enable FA and NetLogin Logging
```bash
# Enable Fabric Attach debug logging
enable log debug-mode
configure log target memory-buffer filter DefaultFilter add fabricattach

# Enable NetLogin debug logging
configure log target memory-buffer filter DefaultFilter add netlogin

# View logs
show log messages
```

#### Trace LLDP Discovery
```bash
# Show LLDP neighbors with FA TLVs
show lldp neighbors detail

# Show FA element discovery events
show log events fabricattach
```

#### Verify Internal State
```bash
# Show FA internal state
show fabric attach statistics

# Show NetLogin session state
show netlogin session detail

# Show port authentication state
show netlogin ports
```

### 7.3 Escalation Criteria

**Escalate to Engineering if**:
- Bypass setting accepted but not applied (configuration vs. runtime mismatch)
- Bypass clients triggering NetLogin authentication attempts
- Crash or memory leak with bypass enabled
- Bypass client list not syncing to standby switch
- Upgrade/downgrade corrupts bypass configuration

**Provide**:
1. `show configuration`
2. `show fabric attach elements`
3. `show netlogin`
4. `show log messages` (last 500 lines)
5. `show tech-support` output
6. Topology diagram with bypass settings

## 8. BEST PRACTICES

### 8.1 Security Recommendations

#### Principle of Least Privilege
- **Enable bypass only for trusted device types** (e.g., infrastructure switches, corporate IP phones)
- **Require authentication for endpoints** (e.g., servers, cameras) - keep bypass OFF
- **Document bypass decisions** in network security policy

#### Defense in Depth
- **Combine bypass with MAC filtering**: Even if bypassing NetLogin, use FA VLAN assignments to segment traffic
- **Monitor bypass client list**: Regularly audit `show netlogin` bypass clients for unexpected devices
- **Use I-SID assignment**: Leverage SPBM I-SID to isolate bypass clients in separate service instances

#### Example Security Policy
```bash
# Trusted: Infrastructure only
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch bypass-netlogin on

# Semi-trusted: Corporate managed devices
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone bypass-netlogin on

# Untrusted: Endpoints require auth
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client server bypass-netlogin off
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera bypass-netlogin off

# Unknown: Default deny (OFF)
```

### 8.2 Deployment Strategy

#### Phased Rollout
1. **Phase 1 - Lab Testing**: Validate bypass with representative devices
2. **Phase 2 - Pilot IDF**: Enable bypass on 1-2 closets, monitor for 1 week
3. **Phase 3 - Campus Expansion**: Roll out to remaining closets
4. **Phase 4 - Optimization**: Adjust bypass settings based on operational data

#### Configuration Management
- **Use consistent naming**: Standard VLAN names across all zero-touch-client configs
- **Document I-SID mappings**: Maintain I-SID allocation spreadsheet
- **Template configurations**: Create standard templates for IDF, MDF, edge switches

#### Example Template (IDF)
```bash
# IDF Standard Template - FA with Selective Bypass
enable fabric attach
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client switch vlan default i-sid 16777216 bypass-netlogin on
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client ip-phone vlan voice i-sid 16777220 bypass-netlogin on
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client camera vlan camera i-sid 16777221 bypass-netlogin off
enable fabric attach ports 1:1-1:48
enable netlogin ports 1:1-1:48 mac
```

### 8.3 Operational Guidelines

#### Change Control
- **Test bypass changes in lab** before production deployment
- **Schedule changes during maintenance windows** for camera/server bypass modifications
- **Validate after changes**: Verify show commands match intended configuration

#### Monitoring and Auditing
- **Daily**: Review bypass client list for unexpected devices
- **Weekly**: Audit bypass configuration vs. security policy
- **Monthly**: Performance analysis - attachment time, authentication failure rates

#### Capacity Planning
- **NetLogin license**: Bypass clients reduce authenticated session count, may free licenses
- **LLDP scaling**: Verify LLDP neighbor count doesn't exceed platform limits
- **VLAN capacity**: Ensure enough VLANs available for zero-touch-client assignments

### 8.4 Integration with Network Management

#### SNMP Monitoring
- Monitor FA element attachment traps
- Track NetLogin authentication traps (should decrease with bypass enabled)
- Alert on unexpected bypass client counts

#### Syslog Integration
- Forward FA and NetLogin logs to SIEM
- Create alerts for:
  - Bypass client attachment failures
  - Unexpected client types in bypass list
  - Rapid bypass client flapping (potential attack)

#### Automation
- **API integration**: Use JSONRPC to query bypass status
- **Ansible playbooks**: Automate bypass configuration across switch inventory
- **Python scripts**: Generate reports from `show fabric attach elements` output

```bash
show fabric attach elements
show fabric attach statistics
show netlogin
show netlogin ports
show netlogin session
```

### 10.2 Client Type to Element Type Mapping

| Client Type (CLI) | Element Type (LLDP TLV) | Description |
|-------------------|------------------------|-------------|
| switch | 5 | Network switch |
| server | 6 (Auth) / 7 (No Auth) | Server |
| router | 4 | Router |
| ip-phone | 9 | VoIP phone |
| camera | 10 | IP camera |
| security-device | 8 | Firewall, IPS |

### 10.3 Default Behaviors

| Setting | Default Value | Behavior |
|---------|---------------|----------|
| bypass-netlogin | OFF | Authentication required |
| NetLogin on port | Disabled | Bypass setting shown but N/A |
| FA element without zero-touch config | No assignment | Element discovered, no VLAN applied |
| NetLogin auth failure | Block | FA attachment prevented |

### 10.4 Platform-Specific Notes

| Platform | Notes |
|----------|-------|
| X670-G2 | Supports all client types |
| X590 | Supports all client types |
| X465 | Supports all client types |
| X440-G2 | Supports all client types |
| X770 | Supports all client types, optimized for high port density |

**Universal**: Bypass-netlogin feature supported on all EXOS platforms running 33.7+

## 11. APPENDIX

### A. Quick Reference Card

**Configure Bypass**:
```bash
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client <type> bypass-netlogin on
```

**Verify Bypass**:
```bash
show fabric attach elements | include Bypass
show netlogin | include "Bypass Clients"
```

**Disable Bypass**:
```bash
configure fabric attach zero-touch-client <type> bypass-netlogin off
```

### C. Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **FA** | Fabric Attach - LLDP-based auto-provisioning protocol |
| **I-SID** | Service Instance Identifier - SPBM service identifier (24-bit) |
| **NetLogin** | EXOS network access control (802.1X, MAC, web auth) |
| **Zero-Touch Client** | Pre-configured FA client type with VLAN/I-SID assignment |
| **Proxy Mode** | FA mode where switch acts as proxy for client devices |
| **Element Type** | LLDP TLV value identifying FA device category |
| **Bypass Client** | FA device exempted from NetLogin authentication |

### D. Acronyms

- **EXOS**: Extreme Networks Operating System
- **FA**: Fabric Attach
- **LLDP**: Link Layer Discovery Protocol
- **MAC**: Media Access Control
- **SPBM**: Shortest Path Bridging - MAC
- **TLV**: Type-Length-Value (LLDP data format)
- **VLAN**: Virtual Local Area Network
- **VSP**: Virtual Services Platform
